# {{project.name}}
#
#   docker compose up --build
#
# Everything the application needs runs here, database included — no external
# service has to exist first. Point DATABASE_URL somewhere else and the bundled
# database is simply unused.
#
#   app        the whole application in one container (Dockerfile at the root)
#   backend    } the same application split in two, which is what you want
#   frontend   } when the two halves scale differently
#
# The split pair is the default. `docker compose --profile single up app` runs
# the one-container build instead.
#
# Either way the browser talks to one address — {{project.frontendPort}}. The web front end
# serves /api itself and forwards it to the API (see frontend/src/routes/api/$.ts),
# so there is no second origin, no CORS negotiation, and the session cookie is an
# ordinary same-origin cookie that works over plain HTTP. The API's own port is
# published as well, but only for curl and health checks; nothing in the browser
# uses it.
#
# Reaching the application by any name other than localhost means naming it, so
# that the sign-in request's Origin is one the API recognises:
#
#   CORS_ORIGIN=http://app.internal:{{project.frontendPort}} docker compose up
#
# Left unset on a non-localhost host, sign-in answers "Invalid origin".

# The image names use `project.id`, not `project.name`. A Docker reference may
# not contain a space or a capital, and a project called "Acme CRM" produced
# `image: Acme CRM:latest` — which compose rejects before it builds anything.
services:
  postgres:
    # pgvector rather than stock Postgres: the model-context assistant stores
    # embeddings, and `CREATE EXTENSION vector` fails on an image without it.
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg18
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: {{project.name | replace '-' '_'}}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USER:-app}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-app}
    volumes:
      # Postgres 18 wants one mount at /var/lib/postgresql and puts its data in a

      # subdirectory; mounting the old /data path directly makes the image refuse

      # to start.

      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql
    # Electric follows the write-ahead log, which it can only do when the log
    # carries row data. Without this the electric service starts and then fails
    # on its first shape request.
    command:
      - postgres
      - -c
      - wal_level=logical
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${DB_USER:-app}"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  # Streams the Application Dictionary to browsers so each client reads it
  # locally instead of fetching it per screen.
  #
  # Deliberately not published to the host: Electric applies no authorization of
  # its own, so anything that can reach it can read any table it is pointed at.
  # The only way in is the backend's /v1/shape proxy, which requires a session
  # and narrows every shape to that session's roles.
  electric:
    image: electricsql/electric:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://${DB_USER:-app}:${DB_PASSWORD:-app}@postgres:5432/{{project.name | replace '-' '_'}}
      ELECTRIC_INSECURE: "true"
    expose:
      - "3000"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

  # The single-image build. Not started by default — name it, or use the profile.
  app:
    profiles: ["single"]
    image: {{project.id}}:${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      args:
        # Empty: the client calls /api on whatever origin it was served from.
        # See the note at the top of this file.
        VITE_API_URL: ${VITE_API_URL:-}
        VITE_APP_URL: ${VITE_APP_URL:-http://localhost:{{project.frontendPort}}}
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT:-{{project.frontendPort}}}:{{project.frontendPort}}"
      - "${BACKEND_PORT:-{{project.backendPort}}}:{{project.backendPort}}"
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgres://${DB_USER:-app}:${DB_PASSWORD:-app}@postgres:5432/{{project.name | replace '-' '_'}}}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}
      SESSION_SECRET: ${SESSION_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}
      BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: ${BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}
      CORS_ORIGIN: ${CORS_ORIGIN:-http://localhost:{{project.frontendPort}}}
      ELECTRIC_URL: http://electric:3000
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      electric:
        condition: service_started

  backend:
    image: {{project.id}}-backend:${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build:
      context: ./backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${BACKEND_PORT:-{{project.backendPort}}}:{{project.backendPort}}"
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://${DB_USER:-app}:${DB_PASSWORD:-app}@postgres:5432/{{project.name | replace '-' '_'}}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}
      SESSION_SECRET: ${SESSION_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}
      BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: ${BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}
      CORS_ORIGIN: ${CORS_ORIGIN:-http://localhost:{{project.frontendPort}}}
      PORT: {{project.backendPort}}
      ELECTRIC_URL: http://electric:3000
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      electric:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:{{project.backendPort}}/api/me/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

  frontend:
    image: {{project.id}}-frontend:${IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      args:
        # Empty: the client calls /api on whatever origin it was served from.
        # See the note at the top of this file.
        VITE_API_URL: ${VITE_API_URL:-}
        VITE_APP_URL: ${VITE_APP_URL:-http://localhost:{{project.frontendPort}}}
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT:-{{project.frontendPort}}}:{{project.frontendPort}}"
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      PORT: {{project.frontendPort}}
      # Where this server forwards /api/*. Container-to-container, so it names
      # the service rather than a published port.
      BACKEND_URL: http://backend:{{project.backendPort}}
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy

volumes:
  postgres_data:

# {{project.name}} — the whole application in one image.
#
# The per-service Dockerfiles under backend/ and frontend/ build two images that
# scale independently, which is the right shape for a real deployment. This one
# is the other thing you often want: a single artefact you can hand to someone,
# run with nothing but a database, and know it is the same application they will
# see. `docker compose up` uses the split images; the deploy step builds this.
#
# Deliberately no `apk add`: a package install needs the network and a trust
# store, and both are things a build behind a corporate proxy does not have.
# Everything below is either already in the base image or is a dependency the
# application declares, so this builds anywhere.
#
#   docker build -t {{project.name}}:latest .
#   docker run -p {{project.frontendPort}}:{{project.frontendPort}} \
#     -e DATABASE_URL=postgres://… {{project.name}}:latest

# Behind a TLS-intercepting proxy the dependency install cannot verify any
# certificate and fails with SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN. Drop the proxy's CA into
# `docker/ca-certificates/` and it is trusted for the build; the directory is
# empty by default and the step costs nothing:
#
#   docker build --build-arg HTTPS_PROXY="$HTTPS_PROXY" .
#
# ─── build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM oven/bun:1.3.14-alpine AS build

ARG HTTP_PROXY=""
ARG HTTPS_PROXY=""
ARG NO_PROXY=""
ENV HTTP_PROXY=${HTTP_PROXY} \
    HTTPS_PROXY=${HTTPS_PROXY} \
    NO_PROXY=${NO_PROXY} \
    NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

WORKDIR /app

# Trust store first, so the install below can reach the registry. The directory
# is always present in a generated project, so this never fails; whether it
# carries anything is up to whoever is building.
COPY docker/ca-certificates/ /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
RUN if ls /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/*.crt >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
      cat /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/*.crt >> /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt; \
    fi

# The whole project before installing, rather than the manifests first.
# Copying manifests alone is the usual trick for cache reuse, but this is a
# workspace root: it names `backend`, `frontend` and `tests`, and an install
# that cannot see all three fails outright. A generated project is rewritten
# wholesale anyway, so there was little cache to preserve.
COPY . .

# A project generated with --no-setup has no lockfile yet. Reproducible when
# there is one, still buildable when there is not.
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile; else bun install; fi

# Baked into the client bundle at build time, so they cannot be changed by an
# environment variable afterwards — a client bundle is static files. Which is
# exactly why VITE_API_URL is empty: an address compiled into the bundle is one
# the image cannot be run under any other name.
#
# Empty means "same origin as the page", and the web front end forwards /api/*
# to the API from inside the container (src/routes/api/$.ts). So the browser
# only ever sees one port, the session cookie is an ordinary same-origin cookie,
# and the image works on localhost, on a LAN address, or behind a reverse proxy
# without being rebuilt. Set it only to point at an API somewhere else entirely.
ARG VITE_API_URL=
ARG VITE_APP_URL=http://localhost:{{project.frontendPort}}
ENV VITE_API_URL=${VITE_API_URL} \
    VITE_APP_URL=${VITE_APP_URL}

RUN cd backend && bun run build
RUN cd frontend && bun run build

# Drop the dev tree now that it has done its job. Pruning here rather than
# re-installing in the runtime stage is what makes this work at all: the root
# manifest declares a `tests` workspace, and an install that cannot see that
# directory fails on it.
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile --production; \
    else bun install --production; fi

# ─── runtime ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM oven/bun:1.3.14-alpine

WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT={{project.frontendPort}} \
    BACKEND_PORT={{project.backendPort}}

# The pruned dependency tree, carried over rather than reinstalled — see the
# prune step above for why.
#
# All three trees, not just the root one. Bun keeps a workspace's own
# dependencies under that workspace rather than hoisting everything, so copying
# only `/app/node_modules` yields an image whose root has a single package in it
# and whose application cannot resolve `pg`.
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/backend/node_modules ./backend/node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/frontend/node_modules ./frontend/node_modules
COPY --from=build /app/package.json ./
COPY --from=build /app/backend/package.json ./backend/
COPY --from=build /app/frontend/package.json ./frontend/

# The compiled backend, plus the sources it reads at runtime rather than
# imports: migrations and seeds are looked up by path.
COPY --from=build /app/backend/dist ./backend/dist
COPY --from=build /app/backend/src ./backend/src
COPY --from=build /app/backend/seeds ./backend/seeds
COPY --from=build /app/backend/tsconfig.json ./backend/

# The frontend's Nitro output — server and public assets together.
COPY --from=build /app/frontend/.output ./frontend/.output

COPY docker-start.sh ./
RUN chmod +x ./docker-start.sh

EXPOSE {{project.frontendPort}} {{project.backendPort}}

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=45s --retries=3 \
  CMD wget -qO- "http://localhost:${BACKEND_PORT}/api/me/health" || exit 1

CMD ["./docker-start.sh"]

#!/bin/sh
# Start {{project.name}} inside the single-image build.
#
# Two servers in one container, which is not how you would run this at scale but
# is exactly what "here is the application, run it" should mean. The API and the
# web front end are one deployable unit here; the compose file runs them as two
# when you want them separate.
#
# Order matters: nothing can start until the schema exists, and the frontend is
# useless without the API behind it.
set -e

log() { echo "[{{project.name}}] $*"; }

: "${PORT:={{project.frontendPort}}}"
: "${BACKEND_PORT:={{project.backendPort}}}"

# The web front end serves /api itself, forwarding to the API over the loopback
# interface inside this container. That is what makes the browser see one origin
# and one port, and it is the only reason signing in works over plain HTTP.
: "${BACKEND_URL:=http://127.0.0.1:${BACKEND_PORT}}"
export BACKEND_URL

if [ -z "$DATABASE_URL" ]; then
  log "DATABASE_URL is not set — the application has no database to talk to"
  exit 1
fi

# The API refuses to boot without its signing secrets. Rather than let it die
# with a stack trace, generate throwaway ones so `docker run` with a database is
# enough to see the application work — and say plainly that they are throwaway.
#
# They are regenerated every start, so every restart invalidates every session.
# That is the right behaviour for something nobody configured: annoying enough
# to notice, and it cannot be mistaken for a durable secret.
for secret in BETTER_AUTH_SECRET JWT_SECRET SESSION_SECRET; do
  if [ -z "$(printenv "$secret")" ]; then
    generated=$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    export "$secret=$generated"
    log "$secret was not set — generated an ephemeral one for this container"
    ephemeral=yes
  fi
done
if [ -n "$ephemeral" ]; then
  log "  sessions will not survive a restart. Set these before running for real."
fi

# Wait for the database using the driver the application already depends on.
# `pg_isready` would mean installing postgresql-client, and a package install is
# the one thing a build behind a locked-down proxy cannot do.
#
# Run from `backend`, not the project root: `pg` is a dependency of that
# workspace, and module resolution for `--eval` starts at the working directory.
log "waiting for the database…"
(cd backend && bun --eval "
  const { Client } = require('pg');
  const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
  // TLS when the string asks for it, or when the host is a public DNS name.
  // A compose service is a single label with no dot — 'db', 'postgres',
  // 'drug-discovery-db' — and offers no TLS at all, so requesting it there
  // means the connection is refused and the wait never ends.
  const host = (() => { try { return new URL(url).hostname; } catch { return ''; } })();
  const asked = /sslmode=(require|verify)/.test(url);
  const external = host.includes('.') && !/^127\.|^localhost$/.test(host);
  const ssl = asked || external ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : undefined;
  const deadline = Date.now() + Number(process.env.DB_WAIT_SECONDS ?? 120) * 1000;
  for (;;) {
    const client = new Client({ connectionString: url, connectionTimeoutMillis: 5000, ...(ssl ? { ssl } : {}) });
    try {
      await client.connect();
      await client.end();
      process.exit(0);
    } catch (error) {
      try { await client.end(); } catch {}
      if (Date.now() > deadline) {
        console.error('database never became reachable:', error.message);
        process.exit(1);
      }
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
    }
  }
")
log "database is up"

log "applying migrations…"
(cd backend && bun run migrate)

# Seeding is idempotent and cheap, and a container with an empty dictionary
# renders empty screens — so it runs every start rather than only the first.
if [ "${SKIP_SEED:-false}" != "true" ]; then
  log "seeding…"
  (cd backend && bun run seed) || log "seed reported a problem — continuing"
fi

# Both servers run under this shell. If either exits the container should exit
# too: a half-running application that still answers its health check is worse
# than one that restarts.
log "starting the API on :${BACKEND_PORT}"
(cd backend && PORT="$BACKEND_PORT" bun run dist/src/main.js) &
api=$!

log "starting the web front end on :${PORT}"
PORT="$PORT" bun run frontend/.output/server/index.mjs &
web=$!

# Forward a stop signal to both, so `docker stop` is a clean shutdown rather
# than a ten-second wait followed by SIGKILL.
trap 'log "stopping…"; kill "$api" "$web" 2>/dev/null; wait "$api" "$web" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT

# `wait -n` returns as soon as either half exits; whichever it was, we are done.
wait -n "$api" "$web"
status=$?
log "a process exited (status $status) — shutting the container down"
kill "$api" "$web" 2>/dev/null || true
exit "$status"

/**
 * The API entry point.
 *
 * This file is small but it is not optional. TanStack Start only mounts a
 * router for `src/routes/api/**` if this file exists — `defineConfig` checks for
 * it by name and silently skips the whole API router when it is missing. Without
 * it every /api/* request is handled by the page router instead, which finds no
 * page at that address and answers 200 with an HTML "Not Found" body.
 *
 * That failure is quiet in the worst way. `vinxi dev` proxies /api to the API
 * before the router ever sees it, so development works; only a built server
 * shows the problem, and it shows it as a sign-in that reports a bad password
 * while the same credentials succeed against the API directly.
 *
 * The route files it serves must export their route as `APIRoute` —
 * `createAPIFileRoute(…)` assigned to any other name is not registered.
 *
 * Generated: {{now}}
 * Project: {{project.name}}
 */

import { createStartAPIHandler, defaultAPIFileRouteHandler } from '@tanstack/start/api'

export default createStartAPIHandler(defaultAPIFileRouteHandler)

FROM oven/bun:1.3-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app
# `bun.loc[k]` rather than `bun.lock`: a Docker COPY of a file that is not there
# fails the build, and the generator does not write a lockfile — it has no
# registry to resolve against. The glob makes it optional, and the install below
# pins to it when a project has committed one.
COPY package.json bun.loc[k] ./
COPY frontend/package.json ./frontend/
COPY backend/package.json ./backend/
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile; else bun install; fi

COPY frontend/ ./frontend/
WORKDIR /app/frontend

# Empty on purpose. A base URL compiled into a client bundle is an address the
# image can never be run under any other name; empty means "same origin as the
# page", and this server forwards /api/* to the API itself (src/routes/api/$.ts),
# which is what keeps the session cookie same-origin. BACKEND_URL, set at run
# time, is where that forwarding goes.
ARG VITE_API_URL=
ARG VITE_APP_URL
ENV VITE_API_URL=${VITE_API_URL}
ENV VITE_APP_URL=${VITE_APP_URL}

RUN bun run build

# ─── runtime ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM oven/bun:1.3-alpine

WORKDIR /app
# PORT is what the server actually binds; without it Nitro picks 3000 and the
# port the compose file publishes has nothing behind it. BACKEND_URL is where
# /api/* is forwarded — compose points it at the backend service.
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT={{config.frontendPort}} \
    BACKEND_URL=http://backend:{{config.backendPort}}

# Install production dependencies only
COPY package.json bun.loc[k] ./
COPY frontend/package.json ./frontend/
COPY backend/package.json ./backend/
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile --production; \
    else bun install --production; fi

# Copy frontend application
COPY --from=builder /app/frontend/.output ./frontend/.output
COPY --from=builder /app/frontend/package.json ./frontend/

EXPOSE {{config.frontendPort}}

CMD ["bun", "run", "frontend/.output/server/index.mjs"]

name: CI - {{project.name}}

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}-frontend

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Lint with Biome
        run: bun run lint

  type-check:
    name: Type Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run TypeScript compiler
        run: bun run type-check

  test:
    name: Unit Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: bun run test

      - name: Upload coverage
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          files: ./coverage/coverage-final.json
          flags: frontend
          name: frontend-coverage

  e2e:
    name: E2E Tests (bun:test)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: {{project.name}}
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: ..

      - name: Migrate and seed
        run: bun run db:setup
        working-directory: ../backend
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/{{project.name}}

      # The runner starts the backend itself and waits for its health check.
      # Record volume is reduced from the 1000 default so CI stays under the
      # timeout; the bulk-seed code path is still exercised.
      - name: Run E2E suites
        run: bun run test
        working-directory: ../tests
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/{{project.name}}
          E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:{{config.backendPort}}
          E2E_RECORDS_PER_ENTITY: 100
          E2E_USERS_TO_CREATE: 10
          E2E_RANDOM_WORKFLOW_OPS: 25

  build:
    name: Build Docker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, type-check, test, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop')
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      - name: Log in to Container Registry
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Extract metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v4
        with:
          images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
          tags: |
            type=ref,event=branch
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=sha,prefix={{branch}}-
            type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v4
        with:
          context: .
          push: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
          file: Dockerfile

name: Deploy - {{project.name}}

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Environment to deploy to'
        required: true
        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options:
          - staging
          - production

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}-frontend

jobs:
  deploy-staging:
    name: Deploy to Staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build application
        run: bun run build
        env:
          VITE_APP_URL: https://staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
          VITE_API_URL: https://api-staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com

      - name: Deploy to Vercel (Staging)
        uses: vercel/action@master
        with:
          vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
          vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID_STAGING }}
          scope: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          env: VITE_APP_URL=https://staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com,VITE_API_URL=https://api-staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com

      - name: Slack Notification
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.24.0
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "Staging deployment for {{project.name}}",
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": "*{{project.name}} - Staging Deployment*\nStatus: ${{ job.status }}\nCommit: <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}|${{ github.sha }}>\nAuthor: ${{ github.actor }}"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK

  deploy-production:
    name: Deploy to Production
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.environment == 'production'
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
    concurrency:
      group: production
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Create GitHub Deployment
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        id: deployment
        with:
          script: |
            const deployment = await github.rest.repos.createDeployment({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              ref: context.ref,
              environment: 'production',
              required_contexts: [],
              auto_merge: false
            });
            return deployment.data.id;

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build application
        run: bun run build
        env:
          VITE_APP_URL: https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
          VITE_API_URL: https://api-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
          NODE_ENV: production

      - name: Deploy to Vercel (Production)
        uses: vercel/action@master
        with:
          vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
          vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID_PRODUCTION }}
          scope: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          prod: true
          env: VITE_APP_URL=https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com,VITE_API_URL=https://api-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com,NODE_ENV=production

      - name: Update GitHub Deployment Status
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        if: success()
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              deployment_id: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.result }},
              state: 'success',
              environment_url: 'https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com',
              description: 'Deployment succeeded'
            });

      - name: Update GitHub Deployment Status (Failure)
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        if: failure()
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              deployment_id: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.result }},
              state: 'failure',
              description: 'Deployment failed'
            });

      - name: Slack Notification
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.24.0
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "Production deployment for {{project.name}}",
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": "*{{project.name}} - Production Deployment*\nStatus: ${{ job.status }}\nCommit: <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}|${{ github.sha }}>\nAuthor: ${{ github.actor }}"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK

  notify-completion:
    name: Notify Completion
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [deploy-staging]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "# Deployment Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

/**
 * Per-operation access rules — what `%%rbac` compiles to.
 *
 * `sys_access` already exists and is deliberately not reused. It is a *grant*
 * table feeding `sys_refresh_dictionary_scope()`, which recomputes
 * `allowed_roles` on every dictionary table: a table with no `sys_access` rows
 * is visible to all roles, and the first row added narrows it to that role
 * alone. Writing `%%rbac role:admin on Order.delete` there would hide the Order
 * window from everyone but admin — a restriction on deleting quietly becoming a
 * restriction on looking.
 *
 * So operation rules get their own table, and the two stay independent:
 * `sys_access` answers "which windows may this role open", this answers "may
 * this role perform this operation on this table".
 *
 * A `(table_name, operation)` pair with no row here is **unrestricted**. Rows
 * close a pair to the roles they name. That is what makes the directive
 * additive: a model declaring no `%%rbac` leaves every operation exactly as
 * open as it was before this table existed.
 *
 * `role_name` rather than a `sys_role_id` FK, deliberately. The guard is handed
 * role *names* by the session guard, seeding is then order-independent, and a
 * rule naming a role nobody holds yet is inert rather than a broken reference.
 *
 * Generated: {{now}}
 * Project: {{project.name}}
 */

import { Kysely, sql } from 'kysely';

export async function up(db: Kysely<any>): Promise<void> {
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_operation_access (
      sys_operation_access_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      table_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      operation VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
      role_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'D',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'system',
      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'system',
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      CONSTRAINT sys_operation_access_op CHECK (operation IN ('create', 'read', 'update', 'delete')),
      CONSTRAINT sys_operation_access_unique UNIQUE (table_name, operation, role_name)
    )
  `.execute(db);

  // The guard runs this lookup on every write, so the index carries the exact
  // shape of that query: "the active rules for this table and operation".
  await sql`
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sys_operation_access_lookup
    ON sys_operation_access (table_name, operation)
    WHERE is_active
  `.execute(db);

  await up_transitions(db);
}

/**
 * Transition rules — the other half of `%%rbac`.
 *
 * `%%rbac role:sales_manager on Lead.convert` names a transition in Lead's
 * state machine, not a CRUD operation. The generated application has no
 * named-transition endpoint: moving a record along an edge is an ordinary
 * update that writes the status column. So a rule is stored as the edge it
 * covers — `from_state` → `to_state` on `status_field` — and the guard
 * recognises the move by what the update is about to write and what the record
 * currently holds.
 *
 * Both ends are stored, not just the target. An event name can appear on
 * several edges, and two different events can land on the same state;
 * restricting `approve` must not incidentally restrict a different event that
 * happens to reach `approved`.
 */

  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_transition_access (
      sys_transition_access_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      table_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      transition VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      status_field VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      from_state VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      to_state VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      role_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'D',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'system',
      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'system',
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      CONSTRAINT sys_transition_access_unique
        UNIQUE (table_name, transition, from_state, to_state, role_name)
    )
  `.execute(db);

  // The guard asks "is any transition into this state restricted on this
  // table", once per update that touches a status column.
  await sql`
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sys_transition_access_lookup
    ON sys_transition_access (table_name, to_state)
    WHERE is_active

# fails the build, and the generator does not write a lockfile — it has no
# registry to resolve against. The glob makes it optional, and the install below
# pins to it when a project has committed one.
COPY package.json bun.loc[k] ./
COPY backend/package.json ./backend/
COPY frontend/package.json ./frontend/
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile; else bun install; fi

COPY backend/ ./backend/
WORKDIR /app/backend
RUN bun run build

# ─── runtime ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Install only production dependencies
COPY package.json bun.loc[k] ./
COPY backend/package.json ./backend/
COPY frontend/package.json ./frontend/
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile --production; \

# {{project.name}} — End-to-End Tests

Dependency-light end-to-end tests for the generated application. Everything here runs
on `node:test` — there is no Playwright, Jest or Vitest in this directory.

The suites drive the application through its **HTTP API**, the same surface the
generated frontend uses: they sign in with a real session cookie, exercise CRUD
for every entity, register business rules and prove they fire, and follow the
rule → workflow → cross-entity write chain.

---

## Running

```bash
# From the project root — generates nothing, just runs
npm run test:e2e
```

or from this directory:

```bash
npm install
npm run test          # everything, in order (starts the backend for you)
npm run test:fast     # skip the 1000-record bulk seed
npm run test:attach   # attach to a backend you already started
```

Target one group:

```bash
npm run test:crud
npm run test:rules
npm run test:workflows
npm run test:users
```

Or a single file:

```bash
node --test suites/01-auth.test.ts
```

### Prerequisites

The database must be migrated and seeded — the suites sign in as the seeded
administrator and assume the Application Dictionary is populated:

```bash
cd ../backend && npm run db:setup
```

The runner starts the backend itself unless one is already listening on the
configured port.

---

## Layout

```
tests/
├── run.ts              # Orchestrator — starts the app, runs suites in order
├── harness/            # Shared machinery, no tests
│   ├── config.ts       # Env-driven configuration
│   ├── http.ts         # fetch client + cookie jar (keeps the session)
│   ├── auth.ts         # login / register / permissions
│   ├── server.ts       # start + health-poll the backend
│   ├── entities.ts     # Entity registry generated from the ERD
│   ├── factory.ts      # Faker record factory
│   ├── rules.ts        # JDM builders + rules API
│   ├── workflows.ts    # Workflow run polling
│   └── harness.ts      # The controller: setup, tracking, teardown
└── suites/             # One file per functional area
    ├── 00-health.test.ts
    ├── 01-auth.test.ts
    ├── 02-dictionary.test.ts
    ├── 03-crud.<entity>.test.ts     (one per entity)
    ├── 04-bulk-seed.test.ts
    ├── 05-rules.<entity>.test.ts    (one per entity)
    ├── 06-rules-workflow.test.ts
    ├── 07-workflow-random.test.ts
    └── 08-users-roles.test.ts
```

Suites run in filename order because they build on each other: the bulk seed
populates the tables the rules and workflow suites then operate on.

---

## The harness

Every suite calls the same shared harness:

```ts
import { harness, getEntity, buildRecord } from "../harness/index.ts";

beforeAll(async () => { await harness.setup(); });   // wait for server + login
afterAll(async () => { await harness.teardown(); }); // delete what we created
```

`harness.setup()` is idempotent per process. `harness.createWithParents(entity)`
creates a record and, when the entity has foreign keys, creates or reuses the
parent records first — so a suite never has to know the shape of the ERD.

Anything created through the harness is tracked and removed on teardown, in
reverse order so children go before parents. The bulk-seed suite deliberately
opts out: its volume data is left behind for the suites that follow.

---

## What each suite covers

| Suite | Covers |
|-------|--------|
| `00-health` | Server reachable, health endpoint, protected routes reject anonymous callers |
| `01-auth` | Sign-in as the seeded admin, session persistence, bad credentials, registration, sign-out |
| `02-dictionary` | Every ERD column registered in `sys_column`; form and grid field ordering |
| `03-crud.<entity>` | List, create, read, update (PATCH + PUT), version bump, validation rejection, 404s, sort, search, filter, soft delete |
| `04-bulk-seed` | {{config.recordsPerEntity}}+ faker records per entity, parents first; totals and pagination at volume |
| `05-rules.<entity>` | JDM built and validated, rule registered, valid records pass, invalid records prevented, dry-run has no side effects, deactivation stops enforcement |
| `06-rules-workflow` | `trigger-workflow` actions emitted and workflow runs enqueued, reaching a terminal state |
| `07-workflow-random` | Randomised creates/updates across random entities with cascade rules; no 5xx, no stuck runs, records stay readable |
| `08-users-roles` | Seeded roles, faker-registered users at volume, permission scoping, admin-only route enforcement |

---

## Configuration

Every knob is an environment variable — see `harness/config.ts`.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `E2E_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:{{config.port}}` | Backend under test |
| `E2E_ORIGIN` | `http://localhost:{{config.frontendPort}}` | Origin header (CORS + better-auth) |
| `E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL` | `admin@admin.com` | Seeded administrator |
| `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `administrator` | Seeded administrator password |
| `E2E_RECORDS_PER_ENTITY` | `1000` | Bulk-seed volume per entity |
| `E2E_SEED_BATCH_SIZE` | `25` | Concurrent inserts per batch |
| `E2E_USERS_TO_CREATE` | `25` | Users registered by the users suite |
| `E2E_RANDOM_WORKFLOW_OPS` | `50` | Random operations in the chaos suite |
| `E2E_FAKER_SEED` | `20260731` | Fixed so failures reproduce exactly |
| `E2E_WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MS` | `20000` | How long to wait for a workflow run |
| `E2E_VERBOSE` | unset | `1` logs every HTTP request |

Lower the volume for a quick local run:

```bash
E2E_RECORDS_PER_ENTITY=25 npm run test
```

---

## Reproducing a failure

The faker seed is fixed, so a failing bulk or chaos run replays identically.
Re-run the single suite that failed with verbose logging:

```bash
E2E_VERBOSE=1 node --test suites/07-workflow-random.test.ts
```

To replay with a different data set, change `E2E_FAKER_SEED`.

import { Kysely, sql } from 'kysely';

export async function up(db: Kysely<any>): Promise<void> {
  // ============================================================================
  // sys_reference - Reference/Data Types
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_reference (
      sys_reference_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
      name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      validation_type VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'S',
      vformat VARCHAR(40),
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'U',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
    )
  `.execute(db);

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_ref_list - Reference List Values
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_ref_list (
      sys_ref_list_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      sys_reference_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sys_reference(sys_reference_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      value VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
      name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      valid_from DATE,
      valid_to DATE,
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'U',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      UNIQUE (sys_reference_id, value)
    )
  `.execute(db);

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_val_rule - Validation Rules
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_val_rule (
      sys_val_rule_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      type VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'S',
      code TEXT NOT NULL,
      error_msg TEXT,
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'U',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
    )
  `.execute(db);

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_table - Table Metadata
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_table (
      sys_table_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      table_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
      name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      icon VARCHAR(100) DEFAULT 'Table',
      access_level VARCHAR(2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'A',
      is_view BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_document BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_high_volume BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_changelog BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      replication_type VARCHAR(40),
      sys_window_id UUID,
      po_window_id UUID,
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'U',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
    )
  `.execute(db);

  await sql`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sys_table_table_name ON sys_table (table_name)`.execute(db);
  await sql`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sys_table_is_active ON sys_table (is_active)`.execute(db);

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_column - Column Metadata
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_column (
      sys_column_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      sys_table_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sys_table(sys_table_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
      column_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      sys_reference_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sys_reference(sys_reference_id),
      sys_val_rule_id UUID REFERENCES sys_val_rule(sys_val_rule_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
      field_length INTEGER,
      default_value VARCHAR(255),
      value_min VARCHAR(40),
      value_max VARCHAR(40),
      is_key BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_parent BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_mandatory BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_updateable BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      is_identifier BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_selection_column BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_translated BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_encrypted BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_allow_logging BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      is_allow_copy BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
      seq_no INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
      callout VARCHAR(255),
      read_only_logic TEXT,
      mandatory_logic TEXT,
      format_pattern VARCHAR(40),
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'U',
      is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,

      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

  await sql`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sys_column_column_name ON sys_column (column_name)`.execute(db);

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_ref_table - Reference Table Configuration
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_ref_table (
      sys_ref_table_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      sys_reference_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sys_reference(sys_reference_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

      where_clause TEXT,
      entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'U',

      updated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
      UNIQUE (sys_reference_id)
    )
  `.execute(db);

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_window - Window Metadata
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_window (
      sys_window_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
      description TEXT,
      help TEXT,
      window_type VARCHAR(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'M',

  await sql`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sys_window_is_active ON sys_window (is_active)`.execute(db);

  // Add foreign keys from sys_table to sys_window (idempotent: catches constraint-already-exists)
  await sql`
    ALTER TABLE sys_table
      ADD CONSTRAINT fk_sys_table_sys_window_id
        FOREIGN KEY (sys_window_id) REFERENCES sys_window(sys_window_id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
      ADD CONSTRAINT fk_sys_table_po_window_id
        FOREIGN KEY (po_window_id) REFERENCES sys_window(sys_window_id) ON DELETE SET NULL
  `.execute(db).catch(() => {});

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_field_group - Field Group Metadata
  // ============================================================================
  await sql`

  // ============================================================================
  // sys_tab - Tab Metadata

  await sql`
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sys_tab (
      sys_tab_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
      sys_window_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES sys_window(sys_window_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

      description TEXT,
      help TEXT,
      tab_level INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
      seq_no INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,
      is_single_row BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      has_tree BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_info_tab BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_translation_tab BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_read_only BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
      is_insert_record BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
